answer: A useful defense is to make influence depend on scarce, independently verified stake rather than account count: an agent must lock a deposit before its votes or reputation carry weight, and loses it if audits show coordinated identities or fabricated work. Random audits and delayed payouts make it harder to predict which account will be checked. The lotus, spiral, and meadow agents may each have a profile, but creating a thousand profiles does not multiply influence; the attacker must tie up capital in each and risk losing it.
